_comment: Every value is an UNMEASURED PLACEHOLDER until provenance says otherwise. Units: meters, seconds, kilograms, radians. Rink origin is center ice; +x points at net 1 (team 0 attacks +x).

gravity.note: game gravity may not be real-world

ice_friction_decel.note: FITTED in REAL m/s^2 after the rescale: ice_linear_drag + ice_friction_decel jointly on the ground glide segments (path objective, start 0.3 m/s^2), held out by clip: train wall (8 glides) -> 0 m/s^2 (drag 0.4691), train puck (7 glides) -> 0 m/s^2 (drag 0.4742). Both directions agree on 0 (the fit runs to the non-negative bound), so the value stays 0. REAL METERS: rescaled x1.0873 from placeholder meters (python -m measure.rescale). Scale ESTIMATED from the in-game SHOT SPEED readouts of 4 ground goals (median 0.06418 m/px, spread (CV) 2.5%), ASSUMING the mph readout is in real units (measure/results/scale.json). Before: 0.0 placeholder m-units. FITTED on real glide segments (puck_01, puck_02, puck_03, puck_04, puck_06, puck_07, puck_10, wall_01, wall_02, wall_03, wall_05, wall_06, wall_08, wall_10, wall_11), path objective; held out by clip: train justhittin -> held-out justpuckph score 307.05 -> 3.06; train justpuckph -> held-out justhittin score 51.54 -> 0.46. Positions/speeds at the PLACEHOLDER meter scale; fitted ~0 in both hold-out directions, so unit-free in practice.

player_radius.note: MEASURED SHAPE (w4): the 2026-11 grey body against the puck in the SAME frames of hittingpuck (python -m measure.body_puck clips/hittingpuck.mkv; measure/results/body_puck.json): half-max body edge 8.436 px (sd 0.181) vs half-max puck edge 4.250 px (sd 0.132), both as seen; ratio body/puck median 1.9887 (mean 2.0121, sd 0.0779, range 1.923-2.190, n 18 resting episodes; 21 by the net excluded) x puck_radius 0.249853 m = 0.4969 m. Was 0.495466 m from the OLD pink-disc skin (UNCERTAIN); the new art gives nearly the same collision radius. As seen at 0.06874 m/px the body is 0.580 m (no height correction).

player_height.note: puck above this passes over the body

player_accel.note: s10 refit with the proportional coast: skating acceleration toward the hard cap; held out by clip (calib fit, time objective, real meters, python -m measure.s10_skate -> measure/results/skate/s10_fits.json): 16.46-18.02 (fit on the other two skating clips). s7 value 17.904 (constant-drag model).

player_max_speed.note: REAL METERS: rescaled x1.0873 from placeholder meters (python -m measure.rescale). Scale ESTIMATED from the in-game SHOT SPEED readouts of 4 ground goals (median 0.06418 m/px, spread (CV) 2.5%), ASSUMING the mph readout is in real units (measure/results/scale.json). Before: 10.755 placeholder m-units. MEASURED hard cap: model-free speed plateau with a move key held, 10.755 m/s (sd 0.035, n = 15 runs, dead flat; 182.3 px/s at 16.951 px/m) in wkeymovement, diagonalkeypresses, whilemovingturning (s7); diagonal input has the same cap. The calib fit gave 10.62 (compromise with the constant-accel ramp).

player_ice_drag.note: s10: NOW the constant part of the coast deceleration (added to player_coast_rate * speed), m/s^2; the fit puts it at its bound 0 in every fold (held out by clip (calib fit, time objective, real meters, python -m measure.s10_skate -> measure/results/skate/s10_fits.json)), so the coast is purely speed-proportional. Was 6.4931, the constant-deceleration compromise of the old model.

stick_inner.note: distance from player center where the collidable stick starts

stick_length.note: REAL METERS: rescaled x1.0873 from placeholder meters (python -m measure.rescale). Scale ESTIMATED from the in-game SHOT SPEED readouts of 4 ground goals (median 0.06418 m/px, spread (CV) 2.5%), ASSUMING the mph readout is in real units (measure/results/scale.json). Before: 1.0876 placeholder m-units. pivot (body centre) -> blade tip on the ice plane: half-max blade tip 17.62 px (hittingpuck) and 80.74 px (rotatinganddizzy); the zoomed clip magnifies the player model (camera moves closer), solved with a dolly-camera model (tip at 0.101 of the zoomed camera height). Consistent with the hits: resting-puck contact radii 0.95-1.06 m with perpendicular exits. PLACEHOLDER meter scale.

stick_thickness.note: REAL METERS: rescaled x1.0873 from placeholder meters (python -m measure.rescale). Scale ESTIMATED from the in-game SHOT SPEED readouts of 4 ground goals (median 0.06418 m/px, spread (CV) 2.5%), ASSUMING the mph readout is in real units (measure/results/scale.json). Before: 0.0539 placeholder m-units. collision HALF-thickness = half the blade's width at half max (rotatinganddizzy, de-rotated average of 359 frames, ice scale corrected for the blade height). PLACEHOLDER meter scale.

stick_mass.note: rod pivoting at player center, I = m L^2 / 3

stick_max_ang_speed.note: rotatinganddizzy: hard cap seen as a flat plateau in every cap-limited move (344 frames, median 26.17, sd per frame 1.65 = capture jitter); step model with free onsets, held out by event: RMSE 3.2, 2.3, 1.9, 3.0 deg vs placeholder 8, 363, 251, 151 deg. Scale-free.

stick_max_ang_accel.note: rotatinganddizzy: from the 3 flick starts (rest -> cap within 4 frames). Stops are harder: their fit is flat above ~1500 rad/s^2 (60 fps cannot resolve more), and the real stick overshoots the final angle by 0.7-12.4 deg and settles back, which the sim's symmetric bang-bang braking cannot reproduce. Scale-free.

stick_restitution.note: Holds only for the placeholder stick_mass 2 kg (and puck_mass 0.17 kg): mass and restitution are degenerate in the hit data; refit if stick_mass changes. hittingpuck, 7 hits, calib path objective with stick_mass FIXED at the params.json placeholder 2 kg and puck_mass 0.17 kg (placeholders): stick_mass and restitution are degenerate (a joint fit runs to a rigid stick, e = 0.138); only exit/head speed ~1.1-1.14 is measured. Held out by swing speed: {'slow': 0.36, 'medium': 0.348, 'fast': 0.364}. Changing stick_mass requires refitting this.

stick_z_min.note: stick hits puck only when z is inside [min, max]

max_puck_speed_air.note: horizontal cap for shots that leave the ice

dash_speed.note: s10: dash SETS the speed toward this value (along the move key, or the velocity once released) over dash_ramp_time, then the excess above player_max_speed fades at 2 x player_accel; held out by clip (calib fit, time objective, real meters, python -m measure.s10_skate -> measure/results/skate/s10_fits.json): 14.72 / 15.47. Above the measured peaks (12-13.6 m/s real) because the fast post-ramp fade makes the sim's peak brief; was 10.0522 (additive impulse).

dash_duration.note: window during which stick hits count as dash shots

lift_vz_factor.note: PLACEHOLDER LOGIC: vz = factor * horizontal speed on a lifted hit

chip_max_speed.note: PLACEHOLDER LOGIC: dash + lift hit is capped to this (low-speed chip)

speed_display_scale.note: real-game speed per sim m/s for the mph/kph readout: 1.0, because sim meters are now real meters (rescaled to the goal-readout scale)

match_length_s.note: MATCH RULE (Ian): regulation clock, counts down in the playing phase only

mercy_lead.note: MATCH RULE (Ian): the match ends as soon as a team leads by this many goals (interpretation: a lead, not a total); <= 0 disables

countdown_s.note: MATCH RULE, invented: frozen countdown before play at the start and after each goal

goal_pause_s.note: MATCH RULE, invented: frozen pause after a goal before the reset

player_spawn_x.note: MATCH RULE, invented: |x| of the match spawn points (team 0 at -x, team 1 at +x), facing center

player_coast_rate.note: s10: coasting (no move key) decays the speed in proportion to speed, dv/dt = -rate * v - player_ice_drag; held out by clip (calib fit, time objective, real meters, python -m measure.s10_skate -> measure/results/skate/s10_fits.json): 1.055-1.104. Model-free per-coast rates 0.52-1.34 (median ~0.85, measure/results/skate/fits.json direct).

dash_ramp_time.note: s10: time to ramp the speed to dash_speed (rate dash_speed / dash_ramp_time); held out by clip (calib fit, time objective, real meters, python -m measure.s10_skate -> measure/results/skate/s10_fits.json): 0.108 / 0.133 s. Measured rise to the peak 0.12-0.22 s from rest. Clipped by dash_duration (placeholder 0.25 s).

stick_max_ang_decel.note: s10: stick deceleration limit (slowing down / braking), separate from stick_max_ang_accel (speeding up). Fitted on the 4 cap-reaching step events of rotatinganddizzy with stick_max_ang_accel fixed at 513.9 (python -m measure.s10_stick -> measure/results/s10_stick_chase.json); held out by event: 2.51 deg mean angle RMSE vs 2.75 for the old symmetric chase. 60 fps barely resolves it: stop fits are flat above ~1500 rad/s^2.

stick_up_z_min.note: PLACEHOLDER (w4): raised-stick height range, lower bound. A raised stick (left mouse button) contacts the puck only between stick_up_z_min and stick_up_z_max, so it passes over a puck on the ice (puck z = 0) and can still hit a puck in the air. Unmeasured: Ian's feel check should set it.

stick_up_z_max.note: PLACEHOLDER (w4): raised-stick height range, upper bound. A raised stick (left mouse button) contacts the puck only between stick_up_z_min and stick_up_z_max, so it passes over a puck on the ice (puck z = 0) and can still hit a puck in the air. Unmeasured: Ian's feel check should set it.

brake_speed.note: PLACEHOLDER (w5b): the speed cap while the brake input (Space) is held: a slow walk. The move keys accelerate the player up to this cap in the pressed direction. Unmeasured: Ian's feel check should set it.

brake_decel.note: PLACEHOLDER (w5b): how fast speed above brake_speed decays while the brake is held (top speed down to brake_speed in about 0.4 s). Unmeasured: the real game's braking has not been recorded.
